To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the projected distributions of mass and galaxies in clusters are similar, while the ICM distributions are quite different in a various ways from those of mass and galaxies.
the distributions of dark matter, galaxies, and ICM are similar to each other for binary clusters, but significantly different for merging clusters.

(1) the mass distribution is overall similar to the galaxy distribution, (2) the ICM distribution is different from the mass distribution, (3) the ICM temperature is higher than the cluster mass, (4) the ICM is not in hydrostatic equilibrium, and (5) the ICM could have been boosted in the on-going and cold front clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the dark matter, I CM, and galaxies associated to cluster formation and evolution, which is one of the most interesting and important issues in cluster cosmology.
the interplay between dark and baryonic matter and the evolution of the ICM in clusters of galaxies.
the interplay among the mass, galaxies, ICM, the cluster environment, and the merger activity in clusters of galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ICM is not in hydrostatic equilibrium with the dark matter, and that the ICM distribution is highly disturbed in on-going and cold front clusters.
the mass and baryon distribution of merging clusters of galaxy is highly irregular, and the baryonic distribution is not necessarily a fair tracer of the underlying dark matter distribution.
the dark matter, galaxies, and ICM are not always well aligned in merging clusters, and the Icm temperature is higher than the cluster mass by a factor of 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass distribution of merging clusters is similar to the galaxy distribution, whereas the ICM distribution is significantly different from both the mass and the galaxy distributions.
the dark matter distribution is similar to the galaxy distribution, whereas the ICM distribution shows a significant difference from both the dark matter and the galaxy distributions.
the ICM is not a faithful tracer of the underlying mass distribution of merging clusters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ICM and galaxy distributions in merging clusters are quite different from each other, and that the ICM is more sensitive to the effects of mergers than the optical galaxy distribution.

the mass, ICM, galaxy distributions, and the global cluster parameters are all different from each other, and that the mass distribution of the cluster is the most regular and smooth among all the distributions, while the ICM distribution is the most irregular.
the mass distribution of merging clusters is not always regular but often irregular, whereas that of binary clusters is regular.
